title: ActiveReg: Information-Driven Active Regional Probing for Partial-to-Full Bone Registration
summary: Accurate bone registration is essential for orthopedic surgical navigation and robotic assistance. In a common workflow, the surgeon needs to identify and probe a number of prescribed locations on the exposed bone surface to obtain data points for registration, which can be difficult and time-consuming under limited surgical exposure. Reducing the number of required points while providing clear probing guidance would ease the surgeon's acquisition task intra-operatively. We present ActiveReg, a closed-loop framework that recommends probing regions rather than individual points, allowing flexibility in the exact contact location. A D-optimal planner that takes into account the already acquired points and the uncertainty of current registration information helps achieve accurate registration with fewer points. An online assessment combines pre-update innovation consistency with uncertainty at predefined surgical task locations improves the reliability of completion decision, without requiring ground truth. Simulations across four anatomical scenarios demonstrated that ActiveReg can achieve competitive accuracy compared with baseline registration methods while using substantially fewer acquired points. Real phantom experiments with optical and electromagnetic tracking demonstrated comparable mean target registration error to the Gradient-SDF framework, using only 24-28 acquired points instead of 771-1263.
tldr: ActiveReg is a closed-loop active regional probing framework for partial-to-full bone registration that recommends flexible probing regions via D-optimal planning and uses uncertainty-based completion assessment, substantially reducing the number of intra-operatively acquired points while maintaining registration accuracy in orthopedic navigation.
tldr_zh: ActiveReg是一种用于骨骼部分到整体配准的闭环主动区域探测框架，通过D-optimal规划推荐灵活的探测区域，并利用不确定性评估完成时机，在保持配准精度的同时大幅减少术中所需采集的点数。
summary_zh: 准确的骨骼配准对于骨科手术导航和机器人辅助至关重要。在常见的工作流程中，外科医生需要在暴露的骨表面上识别并探测若干规定位置以获取配准数据点，这在有限的手术暴露下可能困难且耗时。在减少所需点数的同时提供清晰的探测引导，将有助于外科医生在术中的采集任务。我们提出了ActiveReg，一种闭环框架，它推荐探测区域而非单个点，从而允许精确接触位置具有灵活性。一种考虑已采集点和当前配准信息不确定性的D-最优规划器，有助于用更少的点实现准确配准。在线评估将更新前的新息一致性与预定手术任务位置处的不确定性相结合，在无需真值的情况下提高了完成决策的可靠性。在四种解剖场景中的模拟表明，与基线配准方法相比，ActiveReg能够在显著减少采集点数的同时达到具有竞争力的精度。使用光学和电磁跟踪的真实体模实验表明，其平均目标配准误差与Gradient-SDF框架相当，而仅需采集24-28个点，而非771-1263个点。

title: OA-MAP: Evidence-Grounded Multi-Agent Multimodal Framework for Interpretable Knee Osteoarthritis Progression
summary: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) progression prediction can support patient monitoring, requiring the integration of multimodal data and multidomain expertise. Moreover, isolated risk estimates provide limited insight underlying a prediction. To automate the progression assessment workflow and reduce manual effort while providing interpretable findings and supporting evidence, we present OA-MAP, an autonomous multi-agent framework for evidence-grounded assessment of structural and pain progression in KOA. The system incorporates modality-specific agents including MRI, X-ray, and clinical agents, together with a coordinator agent. This framework can autonomously recruit specialist agents, select tools for prediction and analysis, and retrieve literature as external evidence based on user request and available patient information. An uncertainty-informed human-in-the-loop mechanism enables clinicians to review and correct intermediate findings, triggering recomputation of affected results. We evaluate the prediction models using 600 participants from the FNIH Osteoarthritis Biomarkers Consortium cohort. On the test set of 100 participants, the fusion models achieve AUROCs of 0.80 for structural progression and 0.68 for pain progression. A case study illustrates how OA-MAP combines risk estimates with intermediate findings, cross-modal conflicts, literature support, and uncertainty indicators to support interactive review.
tldr: OA-MAP is a multi-agent multimodal framework for interpretable knee osteoarthritis progression prediction, integrating MRI, X-ray, clinical data, literature evidence, and an uncertainty-informed human-in-the-loop review mechanism, with fusion model AUROCs of 0.80 for structural and 0.68 for pain progression.
tldr_zh: OA-MAP 是一个用于可解释膝骨关节炎进展预测的多智能体多模态框架，整合 MRI、X 射线、临床数据、文献证据以及不确定性知情的人机协同审查机制，融合模型在结构进展和疼痛进展上的 AUROC 分别为 0.80 和 0.68。
summary_zh: 膝骨关节炎(KOA)进展预测可支持患者监测，这需要整合多模态数据和跨领域专业知识。此外，孤立的风险估计对预测结果背后的深层机制所提供的洞察十分有限。为自动化进展评估工作流程、减少人工操作，同时提供可解释的发现和支持性证据，我们提出了OA-MAP——一种用于KOA结构和疼痛进展证据化评估的自主多智能体框架。该系统整合了包括MRI、X射线和临床智能体在内的模态专用智能体，以及一个协调智能体。该框架可根据用户请求和现有患者信息，自主招募专家智能体、选择预测与分析工具，并检索文献作为外部证据。一种基于不确定性感知的人机协同机制使临床医生能够审查和纠正中间发现，并触发受影响结果的重新计算。我们使用FNIH骨关节炎生物标志物联盟队列中的600名参与者对预测模型进行评估。在100名参与者的测试集上，融合模型在结构进展方面实现了0.80的AUROC，在疼痛进展方面实现了0.68的AUROC。一项案例研究展示了OA-MAP如何将风险估计与中间发现、跨模态冲突、文献支持和不确定性指标相结合，以支持交互式审查。

title: ActiveMedAgent: Cost-Aware Trajectory Learning for Multimodal Medical Diagnosis
summary: Clinical diagnosis is inherently sequential: clinicians escalate from cheap to costly tests only when additional evidence is expected to resolve diagnostic uncertainty. We present ActiveMedAgent, a framework that brings this cost-aware sequential logic to multimodal medical AI. Given a frozen, API-accessed vision-language model, ActiveMedAgent tracks probability distributions over candidate diagnoses and scores each acquisition by its per-step diagnostic utility minus cost. A lightweight MLP controller is then trained offline on these scored trajectories, learning when to request additional evidence and when to commit. Across three commonly used benchmarks, trajectory-based policy learning consistently outperforms both unguided acquisition and full-modality baselines. Notably, we identify an information overload effect. In 175 cases, the agent produces a correct diagnosis with fewer channels while the full-modality baseline fails, showing that learning what to omit can be as important as learning what to acquire.
tldr: ActiveMedAgent trains an MLP controller on cost-adjusted diagnostic utility scores to decide which modalities to acquire for a frozen multimodal VLM, improving accuracy while reducing channel usage on medical diagnosis benchmarks and revealing an information overload effect.
tldr_zh: 提出ActiveMedAgent，通过基于诊断效用与采集成本的轨迹训练轻量级MLP控制器，决定多模态医疗诊断中是否继续获取检查，在多个基准上优于全模态基线，并发现信息过载效应。
summary_zh: 临床诊断本质上具有序贯性：临床医生只有在预期额外证据能解决诊断不确定性时，才会从廉价检查逐步升级到昂贵检查。我们提出ActiveMedAgent，一个将这种成本感知的序贯逻辑引入多模态医学人工智能的框架。给定一个冻结的、通过API访问的视觉-语言模型，ActiveMedAgent跟踪候选诊断上的概率分布，并根据每步诊断效用减去成本对每次信息获取进行评分。随后，一个轻量级MLP控制器在这些评分轨迹上离线训练，学习何时请求额外证据以及何时做出最终诊断。在三个常用基准上，基于轨迹的策略学习持续优于无引导获取和全模态基线。值得注意的是，我们发现了一种信息过载效应：在175个病例中，智能体用更少的信息渠道即做出正确诊断，而全模态基线却失败，这表明学会省略什么与学会获取什么同样重要。
